Desk rules for staff rotas
This section describes how the desk handles it

Companion Animal Travel Desk procedures

The purpose of this section is to guide staff in the calm, consistent handling of companion animal travel arrangements from booking through pickup. Staff should welcome each traveler in a reassuring tone, confirm the stated itinerary, and coordinate with the welcome team so every animal is prepared for boarding in an orderly way. The senior coordinator makes daily service decisions, and all staff are expected to follow those directions without delay.

When a booking includes a bird, staff must apply the current acceptance standard before any space is held or any onward step is confirmed. <<FACT F077>> The traveler should then be advised that the desk will continue with the remaining checks only after the animal is accepted under the usual process, and the record should remain clear and complete. If an issue is found, the matter should be escalated at once to the senior coordinator.

For rabbit travel, staff must review the crate condition, the fit of the animal within the crate, and the combined load before confirming carriage. <<FACT F064>> If the arrangement is suitable, the desk may proceed with the booking notes and handover instructions. If it is not suitable, staff should advise the traveler with courtesy and keep the discussion focused on safe travel, not convenience.

All desk communication must remain warm, professional, and precise. Staff should avoid promising exceptions, should not alter welfare instructions without approval, and should ensure that any special feeding, rest, or pickup notes are passed to the next team in the chain. Where travelers arrive with concerns, the desk should respond promptly, explain the next step in plain terms, and preserve a steady and respectful tone throughout.

Any uncertainty about animal readiness, crate acceptability, or boarding sequence must be referred to the senior coordinator without hesitation. For any unresolved case, contact the senior coordinator through the internal desk channel.
